text:
maria-cs: customer reports a billing delta: invoice shows ~3.2K embedding units charged for a weekly bulk run but our dashboard shows ~1.6K vectors created. They uploaded via our async bulk/manifest path. Customer insists they didn't change batch size or model. Can someone triage?

jason-eng: sorry seeing this now — can you paste the request_id or sample manifest entry? async bulk jobs make the metering flow a bit more complex (manifest -> chunking -> worker retries).

maria-cs: request_id: run_20260215_acctXYZ_01 (shared over DM). Customer provided a sanitized manifest line: `{"s3_uri": "s3://cust-bucket/embeds/part-0001.jsonl", "meta": {"batch_size": 256}}` — they also included the client-side payload snippet: ```json
POST /v1/embeddings/bulk
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v2",
  "truncate": "end",
  "batch_size": 256,
  "manifest_uri": "s3://cust-bucket/embeds/manifest.jsonl"
}
```

tara-billing: billing side pulled the invoice lines and we have entries stamped to worker-queue-7 for request run_20260215_*. The invoice shows 3248 embedding units billed. Our dashboard's aggregate shows 1624 vectors produced for that account during the same time window. Two hypotheses: 1) double-count from retries/partial-success, 2) different accounting for pairwise/rerank operations if the customer mixed rerank calls in the job.

kevin-ml: quick note — if inputs are truncated to zero-length (all tokens removed) we sometimes emit a 1-dummy vector (legacy behavior) which could inflate counts if a retry path resends chunks. Also pairwise rerank counts as N*M if the rerank endpoint was used — but the manifest shows embeddings endpoint.

arnold-support-bot: log snippet attached from ingestion pipeline: `INGEST:event=manifest_queued request=run_20260215_acctXYZ shard=7 entries=13` then `WORKER:chunk_start request=run_20260215_acctXYZ chunk_id=7 items=256` then `WORKER:retry reason=timeouts chunk_id=7 retry=1 items=256` then `METER:emb_count account=acctXYZ vectors=512 request=run_20260215_acctXYZ` (repeated).

jason-eng: that pattern suggests chunk-level retries where each retry was fully recounted. Our metering should be idempotent keyed by (request,chunk_id,attempt) but it looks like the attempt id wasn't stable so retries got new counts. I'll open infra ticket. Can someone toss the job trace id to infra?

sre-ops: got it. Creating infra-1234. Initial root cause hypothesis: the worker-side metering ack was always sent before the database transaction that recorded the worker's attempt id committed. On retry the system saw no prior attempt and recounted. That fits the numbers: 13 entries * 256 items ~= 3328 expected accounting events if retries duplicated some chunks.

maria-cs: customer asks for repro steps — they want to know if they did anything wrong or if we overcharged. They also asked for a one-time credit if we confirm duplicate counts. They can repro locally if we provide a curl example.

jason-eng: repro (internal): run a manifest with a few large chunks and simulate a transient worker timeout by killing the worker process partway through chunk. Example to reproduce:```bash
# create manifest with two entries that will be split into chunks
echo '{"s3_uri":"s3://test/partA.jsonl","meta":{"batch_size":256}}' > manifest.jsonl
echo '{"s3_uri":"s3://test/partB.jsonl","meta":{"batch_size":256}}' >> manifest.jsonl
# kick off async job
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/bulk -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @manifest.jsonl
# on worker node: kill -9 <pid> while chunk is processing to force retry
```

kevin-ml: addendum: to verify whether truncation is producing dummy vectors, check the preprocessor logs for `input_tokens=0` or `truncated=true && post_truncate_len==0`. If those are present, we might be generating canonical placeholder vectors which would increase counts. But here logs show full-sized items per chunk, so placeholder vectors unlikely.

tara-billing: propose interim remediation: 1) issue a provisional credit for the delta (invoice vs dashboard) while infra debugs, 2) run a targeted replay of the metering pipeline for run_20260215_acctXYZ to compute definitive counts. Approve?

sre-ops: +1 on replay. I'm scheduling a replay window, and will run `billing-replay --request run_20260215_acctXYZ --fix-idempotency` in dry-run first.

maria-cs: customer responded: they'd accept a provisional credit and will wait for final reconciliation. They asked for ETA.

jason-eng: ETA: infra triage and one replay run within 24 hours, patch to worker metering within 72 hours if replay confirms duplicate counting. We'll follow up with the final count and credit amount.

arnold-support-bot: (automated) ticket infra-1234 created and assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://redwood.internal/t/infra-1234

kevin-ml: temporary mitigation idea: adjust metering pipeline to dedupe by (request_id, chunk_id) for any observed counts in the last 48h if attempt_id missing — safe stopgap to avoid future transient duplicates while we fix root cause. Not ideal long-term but low-risk.

tara-billing: I drafted a credit memo for the provisional amount equal to invoice - dashboard = 1624 units and assigned to acctXYZ pending replay results.

maria-cs: thanks all — I'll relay the provisional credit and repro steps to the customer. Please tag me when the replay completes so I can send final reconciliation. :thumbsup:

jason-eng: will do. logging follow-ups in infra-1234 and will paste final replay summary back in this thread.

sre-ops: replay complete (dry-run): results show 1580 unique vectors after dedupe heuristics; counted events in invoice pipeline were 3248. Real delta 1668. Scheduling fix and final accounting run now.

maria-cs: acknowledged, forwarding to customer and closing the loop once final invoice adjustment posted.
